records.title: ELOHIM
records.meaning: Biblical Hebrew divine title. Cross-reference in the creator's polarity matrix without equating it with ELOHER.
records.note: Original 21-file November 2 recovery dossier includes Semitic-name research and the Elohim/Eloher comparison.

records.title: EL / ELOAH / ELAH / ILAH / ALLAH
records.variant: Elohei, Eloah, El, Elah, Ilah, Allah
records.meaning: Related or compared Semitic divine-name spellings from the owner's archived research. Individual lexical histories and languages must be examined separately.
records.note: Not proof that every spelling has the same grammatical meaning or that creator term ELOHER is historical.

records.title: ELLA
records.meaning: Ella as a feminine given name; a name entry is not a religious term by default.
records.note: Requested exactly as Ella's; keep proper-name hits distinct from Spanish grammar and EL + LA wordplay.

records.title: ella
records.meaning: Spanish ella is a third-person feminine singular pronoun: she or her.
records.note: The owner archive's Spanish-language The Twinkling manuscript contains ELLA as ordinary grammar; it is not automatically proof of an Elohim connection.

records.title: EL + LA / ELLA
records.meaning: Creator-driven segmentation and sound comparison of EL, LA and ELLA.
records.note: Keep as interpretive search link, not a verified shared etymology with Elohim.

records.title: EVANGELIST
records.meaning: Greek New Testament title for a bearer or proclaimer of good news; lexical origin does not guarantee that an individual's actions are good.
records.note: Strong's G2099: Acts 21:8, Ephesians 4:11 and 2 Timothy 4:5.

records.title: EVANGELIST (not good)
records.meaning: The owner explicitly marks Evangelist as 'not good'. Preserve this assessment exactly and separately from lexical etymology.
records.note: This classification is an authored evaluative position, not an objective property of every evangelist.

records.title: Philip the evangelist
records.meaning: An independently cataloged New Testament figure titled the evangelist.
records.note: Owner Bible A–Z reference index contains Philip evangelist; do not confuse with Philip the apostle or assert personal wrongdoing.

records.title: EVE — FEMALE
records.meaning: Eve, the Genesis female figure; Genesis 3:20 describes her as mother of all living.
records.note: Biblical narrative is separate from authored mythology, modern persons and time/architecture words.

records.title: EVE — BAT / BANOT / EM → ME
records.variant: EVE - God’s first BAT - aka daughter
records.meaning: Owner-authored Eve model: BAT = daughter, BANOT = daughters; EVE is EM, left-to-right reversal ME; mother of all BATS in the user's symbolic narrative.
records.note: Hebrew bat/batot language and the user's authored family formula must remain distinct from scriptural verbatim claims; neither replaces Eve's own recorded name.

records.title: Adam and Eve Tabor
records.variant: Adam Ape and Eve Ape Tabor
records.meaning: The Tabor Secret Society / two-origins family-saga fiction includes Adam and Eve Tabor and Adam Ape and Eve Ape Tabor.
records.note: Original fiction is not a documented family genealogy or the Genesis historical record.

records.title: eve_vector_gradient
records.meaning: Software attribute for an initialization quantity in a Tabor simulation, explicitly named EVE.
records.note: Recovered Oct 21 2026 engine text; code-like source contains inconsistent labels and is not certified production-safe.

records.title: EAVE / EAVES — HOUSE
records.meaning: Projecting lower edge of a roof. Historical Old English efes described the eaves of a house.
records.note: Eave/eaves and Eve are distinct words with different linguistic origins; preserve as a sound/visual comparison.

records.title: EVE — BEFORE NIGHT
records.meaning: Old English æfen lineage; evening or the time before darkness.
records.note: The user's 'time before night' meaning is grounded in historical use; unrelated to Biblical Chavvah's etymology.

records.title: EVE — BEFORE AN EVENT
records.variant: Christmas Eve / eve of an event
records.meaning: The evening or day immediately before a festival, holiday, or important event; also figuratively the moment before something begins.
records.note: An extended English sense of time-eve, not a reference to the woman or a house's roof.
